<section id="gy-location-hero">

  <div class="gy-location-hero-content">

    <span class="gy-location-kicker">
      California Food Forests &amp; Edible Landscapes
    </span>

    <h1>
      Growing Food in California
    </h1>

    <p>
      Explore community gardens, food forests, farms, and edible landscapes
      across California while discovering how coastal influence, dry summers,
      winter rainfall, heat, and local microclimates shape what people grow.
    </p>

  </div>

</section>


<div class="gy-location-main">

  <div class="gy-location-inner">


    <!-- GROWING IN CALIFORNIA -->
    <section class="gy-section">

      <div class="gy-growing-layout">

        <div class="gy-growing-copy">

          <div class="gy-section-heading">

            <span class="gy-section-label">
              Growing in California
            </span>

            <h2>
              A State Defined by Climate Diversity
            </h2>

          </div>

          <p>
            California contains an enormous range of growing environments.
            Coastal communities can have mild temperatures and strong marine
            influence, inland valleys experience much greater summer heat,
            mountain regions have true winter cold, and Southern California
            includes climates capable of supporting an unusually broad mix of
            temperate, subtropical, and Mediterranean crops.
          </p>

          <p>
            Much of the state is characterized by dry summers and wetter
            winters, making water management a defining part of edible
            landscape design. In many areas, irrigation is essential through
            the warm season even when temperatures are moderated by the coast.
          </p>

          <p>
            California’s diversity also creates exceptional opportunities.
            Citrus, avocado, stone fruit, figs, grapes, pomegranates, loquats,
            mulberries, persimmons, and many other crops can thrive in the
            right region, while warmer parts of Southern California allow
            growers to experiment with mango, banana, guava, cherimoya,
            passion fruit, and other subtropical species.
          </p>

        </div>


        <aside class="gy-growing-note">

          <strong>
            About These California Tours
          </strong>

          <p>
            The Green Yard currently has one California tour, featuring New
            Roots Community Farm in San Diego. Expanding the California tour
            library is a priority, so this page is designed to grow as more
            community gardens, food forests, farms, and edible landscapes are
            filmed across the state.
          </p>

        </aside>

      </div>

    </section>


    <!-- CLIMATE SNAPSHOT -->
    <section class="gy-section">

      <div class="gy-section-heading">

        <span class="gy-section-label">
          Climate Snapshot
        </span>

        <h2>
          California Growing Conditions
        </h2>

        <p>
          California is too diverse for one climate label. These cards
          summarize broad patterns while recognizing that conditions can
          change dramatically between the coast, inland valleys, mountains,
          deserts, and different parts of the state.
        </p>

      </div>


      <div class="gy-climate-grid">

        <div class="gy-climate-card">
          <span>Climate</span>
          <strong>Highly Variable</strong>
          <p>
            Mediterranean, coastal, desert, mountain, and inland climates all
            occur within the state.
          </p>
        </div>

        <div class="gy-climate-card">
          <span>Growing Season</span>
          <strong>Long in Many Regions</strong>
          <p>
            Coastal and Southern California locations can support food
            production through much of the year.
          </p>
        </div>

        <div class="gy-climate-card">
          <span>Summer</span>
          <strong>Dry &amp; Regionally Hot</strong>
          <p>
            Coastal areas may stay mild while inland locations can experience
            intense heat and high irrigation demand.
          </p>
        </div>

        <div class="gy-climate-card">
          <span>Winter</span>
          <strong>Mild to Cold</strong>
          <p>
            Southern coastal areas are often mild, while inland and
            high-elevation regions can experience significant frost or snow.
          </p>
        </div>

        <div class="gy-climate-card">
          <span>Water</span>
          <strong>Seasonal &amp; Valuable</strong>
          <p>
            Dry summers make irrigation, soil moisture conservation, and
            drought-aware design important in many regions.
          </p>
        </div>

        <div class="gy-climate-card">
          <span>Major Advantage</span>
          <strong>Crop Diversity</strong>
          <p>
            The state supports everything from cool-climate fruit to
            subtropical crops depending on location and microclimate.
          </p>
        </div>

      </div>

    </section>


    <!-- OPPORTUNITIES + CHALLENGES -->
    <section class="gy-section">

      <div class="gy-section-heading">

        <span class="gy-section-label">
          The Growing Reality
        </span>

        <h2>
          Why Grow Food in California?
        </h2>

      </div>


      <div class="gy-opportunity-grid">

        <div class="gy-opportunity-card positive">

          <h3>
            Growing Opportunities
          </h3>

          <ul>
            <li>Exceptional range of climates and edible crop possibilities</li>
            <li>Long growing seasons in many coastal and southern regions</li>
            <li>Strong potential for citrus, avocado, grapes, figs, and stone fruit</li>
            <li>Warm Southern California microclimates support subtropical fruit</li>
            <li>Large gardening and farming communities create opportunities for shared knowledge</li>
          </ul>

        </div>


        <div class="gy-opportunity-card challenge">

          <h3>
            Growing Challenges
          </h3>

          <ul>
            <li>Water availability and irrigation needs during dry summers</li>
            <li>Extreme heat in inland valleys and desert regions</li>
            <li>Wildfire, smoke, wind, and changing weather patterns in some areas</li>
            <li>Cool coastal conditions can limit heat-loving crops</li>
            <li>Conditions vary so widely that plant advice must be location-specific</li>
          </ul>

        </div>

      </div>

    </section>


    <!-- WHAT GROWS HERE -->
